context.focus: Rethinking work, a switch, or growth

meta.disclaimer: Beta, accuracy still being checked. Everything shown in Marg is provisional and for guidance only; always double-check every detail (fees, eligibility, dates, links) against the official source before you rely on it or make a decision.

options.name: Upskill in your current field
options.summary: Deepen expertise where you already are, advanced certifications, a specialisation, or a senior-track skill, to grow without changing domain.
leads_to: Higher pay in the same field
A stronger base before any later pivot
options.keeps_open: Lowest-disruption path; compounds what you already have.

eligibility.text: Anyone currently working who wants depth over change. No entry barrier.

approx_cost_inr.note: Often employer-funded; self-paid certifications vary widely.

options.honest_notes: Underrated: growth in place is often faster and safer than a full switch. Weigh it honestly against the urge to start over.

human_touchpoint.idea: Story from someone who leveled up without switching.

options.name: Pivot into tech / data
options.summary: Move toward software, data, analytics or product via structured reskilling, bootcamps, certifications, or a guided self-study path.
options.keeps_open: Broad demand; many adjacent roles if the first target doesn't fit.

eligibility.text: Open to career changers; aptitude and consistent practice matter more than a prior tech degree.

where_in_bangalore.note: Verify placement claims, this space has many over-promising providers.

approx_cost_inr.note: Free/low-cost self-study up to expensive bootcamps; verify outcomes before paying.

options.honest_notes: Real, but the 'quit and bootcamp' story is survivorship-biased. Test interest with a small project first; keep income while you transition.

human_touchpoint.idea: Story from a non-tech professional who switched to data/dev.

options.name: Management / leadership route
options.summary: Grow toward people-leadership or general management, via an MBA, executive education, or moving into a lead role on the job.
options.keeps_open: Opens leadership across industries; not all of it needs a degree.

eligibility.text: Some routes (executive MBA) expect a few years of experience; on-the-job leadership needs none.

approx_cost_inr.note: On-the-job: low. Executive MBA: can be very expensive, weigh ROI honestly.

options.honest_notes: A degree is one route, not the only one. Many strong managers grow in-role, try leading before you spend on a programme.

human_touchpoint.idea: Story from someone who moved into management without an MBA.

options.name: Start your own venture
options.summary: Build a business or product of your own, full-time, or as a side venture you grow before leaving a job.
leads_to: Later re-entry to a role with venture experience
options.keeps_open: Highest autonomy and upside; also highest variance.

eligibility.text: No barrier to starting; success depends on demand, runway and resilience.

approx_cost_inr.note: Highly variable; protect a financial runway before going full-time.

options.honest_notes: Be honest about runway and dependants. Many start as a side venture and only leave the job once it's proven, a valid, lower-risk route.

human_touchpoint.idea: Story from someone who bootstrapped a venture while employed.

options.name: Stable / public sector move
options.summary: Shift toward stability, government roles, PSUs, or established sectors, often via competitive exams or lateral moves.
options.keeps_open: Security and predictability; some routes have age limits worth checking.

eligibility.text: Varies widely by exam/role, several have age and qualification limits. Verify per specific exam.

where_in_bangalore.note: Illustrative; confirm current eligibility and age limits.

approx_cost_inr.note: Low course cost; the real cost is prep time and opportunity cost.

options.honest_notes: Stability is a real value, not a lesser choice. But check age limits early, some doors close by the late 30s.

human_touchpoint.idea: Story from someone who moved from private to public sector mid-career.

options.name: Freelance / independent consulting
options.summary: Take your existing expertise independent, consulting, contracting or freelancing, for flexibility and control over your work.
options.keeps_open: Flexibility and higher day-rates; trades away salary stability.

eligibility.text: Best with a few years of a marketable skill and some network to start from.

approx_cost_inr.note: Low to start; budget for irregular income early on.

options.honest_notes: Freedom comes with irregular income and self-marketing. Many start on the side to build a client base before going full independent.

human_touchpoint.idea: Story from someone who went independent from a salaried role.

options.name: Territorial Army (part-time service)
options.summary: Serve the nation part-time as a Territorial Army officer while keeping your civilian job or business, annual training and short embodiment periods, without leaving your career.
leads_to: Purpose and service alongside your career
Leadership and discipline that carry back into your work
options.keeps_open: You keep your day job, the TA is a parallel commitment, not a career change.

eligibility.text: Gainfully employed or self-employed Indian citizens, typically 18-42, graduate, medically fit. Selection is via a written test and an SSB-style interview.

options.duration: Ongoing, part-time (annual training plus short embodiment)

where_in_bangalore.note: Illustrative; confirm current eligibility and units.

approx_cost_inr.note: No course cost, you're paid for training and embodiment periods.

options.honest_notes: A meaningful way to serve without giving up your career but selection is competitive and there are fitness and age limits. It is not a full-time income.

human_touchpoint.idea: Story from a working professional who serves in the Territorial Army.

specialized_pathways.name: Teaching, training or coaching
specialized_pathways.summary: Turn hard-won experience into teaching, corporate training, mentoring or coaching, as a second act or a portfolio addition.
specialized_pathways.frame: A meaningful pivot for those drawn to helping others grow. Coaching credentials vary a lot in quality, verify recognition before paying for one.

eligibility.text: Depends on the route; domain experience is the main asset.

specialized_pathways.honest_notes: Verify any coaching 'certification' carefully, it's a space with many low-value paid programmes.

specialized_pathways.name: Social sector / purpose-driven work
specialized_pathways.summary: Move toward nonprofit, development, or impact-focused work, often a pay trade-off for greater meaning.
specialized_pathways.frame: For a values-led shift. Be honest about the pay change and plan for it; meaning and money both matter.

eligibility.text: Varies; transferable professional skills are in demand in the sector.

specialized_pathways.honest_notes: Genuine demand for professional skills in the social sector; weigh the income change realistically.

next_horizon_steps: Name the leadership you want (people-manager, tech-lead, general management).
Start leading where you are, a project, a small team, a cross-functional effort.
Add a targeted credential ONLY if a specific door needs it.
pathways.honest_cost_effort: Mostly time and visible ownership, not money, unless you choose an executive programme, which is a real expense to justify.
pathways.what_if_it_changes: Leadership skills transfer everywhere, the effort is not wasted if the destination shifts.

next_horizon_steps: Test the interest with a small real project before committing money.
Pick a structured path (certificate/bootcamp/guided self-study) that fits your runway.
Transition while keeping income where possible; target adjacent roles first.
pathways.honest_cost_effort: 6-18 months of consistent effort; cost ranges from near-zero self-study to expensive bootcamps, verify outcomes before paying.
adjacent_destinations: Tech-adjacent roles in your current domain
pathways.what_if_it_changes: Digital skills strengthen almost any career, so partial progress still pays off.

next_horizon_steps: Reflect honestly on why, and on your financial runway and dependants.
Validate demand small and cheap before leaving a job.
Grow it on the side until it can carry you, if you can.
pathways.honest_cost_effort: High variance and real personal risk; the biggest cost is runway and resilience, not just capital.
adjacent_destinations: Return to a role with venture experience
pathways.what_if_it_changes: Even a venture that doesn't last builds rare, transferable skills, not a dead end.

pathways.ambition: Find better balance or more meaning
next_horizon_steps: Get specific: is it hours, autonomy, purpose, or the work itself?
Consider adjacent moves, same field, better setup, before a full switch.
Explore purpose-led or flexible routes that fit your finances.
pathways.honest_cost_effort: Often less about money than about trade-offs in income, status or security, name the trade-off you're willing to make.
adjacent_destinations: A calmer role in the same field
pathways.what_if_it_changes: Clarity about what you actually want is the real outcome, it holds even if the path changes.
